newsitem.title: UK: UK outlines changes to building societies bill.
newsitem.headline: UK outlines changes to building societies bill.

text.p: British Economic Secretary Angela Knight on Wednesday outlined details of changes she is proposing to the government's draft Building Societies bill following consultation since March with interested parties.
She said in a written parliamentary answer that the final version of the bill would be published shortly.
"This balanced set of measures will guard against disruption while safeguarding key rights of members," Knight said.
-- Takeover protection under the 1986 act prevents anyone from holding more than 15 percent of a society that has converted to Plc status for five years following conversion.
Knight proposes allowing this protection to lapse if, during the five years, the converted society takes over another financial institution, or if its shareholders vote to waive it.

-- societies will be able to ensure that special general meetings do not interfere with the normal cycle of business. They will not be under a statutory obligation to hold a SGM within the three months before and one month after their EGM.
-- Only members of the building society of at least two years' standing will be allowed access to the company's register.
-- The bill will retain powers to strengthen membership conditions in the event of a society being seriously disrupted.
-- Societies will be allowed to send members a short version of the conversion statement when seeking Plc status.
-- Simpler rules to permit ailing societies, in extreme circumstances, to be rescued or taken over without a full vote of its members.

-- The bill would also contain an enabling power to merge, at some point in the future, the banks' deposit and societies' investor protection schemes. Knight said this was solely a contingency provision, should it become necessary in future.
The opposition Labour Party welcomed the government's decision to proceed with the bill and said it should not meet problems over availability of parliamentary time.
But Shadow Economic Secretary to the Treasury Mike O'Brien attacked ministers for not listening to pleas by societies for a two-year membership qualification.
However, Knight said measures within the bill would prove more effective against speculators than such a qualification rule.

"In our recent consultation it came across very strongly that societies were concerned about carpetbaggers. These new plans are far more effective than any extension to the two year rule could have been," Knight said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
